narrative.overview:
A records room after hours. One warm light falls from above, onto brass fittings and parchment labels; everything else sits in a warm, deep dark. The museum's job is to hold other people's history carefully, so the design stays out of the way of the artifacts. The light at the top of every page is literal: a faint brass radial glow from above the masthead (6% brass, fading by mid-page), the only source of "depth" anywhere on the site. Pages read like placards in a gallery, never like posters: quiet, labelled, exact.

The system has two registers and keeps them apart. A serif reads (prose, headings, the body of every page), and a monospace labels (kickers, navigation, table headers, dates, chips, and the verbatim documents themselves, which keep their source's typewritten feel). Density is generous for reading and tight for rows: one 760px reading column, an 18px body at 1.65, and one shared 16px row size for every list and table on the site.

It is plain CSS in one file, `style.css`, with every value read from tokens on `:root`; no framework, no build step, no web fonts, and no inline styles anywhere (the validator refuses a `style=` attribute). Tens of thousands of generated pages inherit the whole look by linking that one file, so the system changes in one place or not at all.
keyCharacteristics: Two themes that follow the visitor's device until they choose: the lamplit dark (warm near-black grounds, parchment text, one gold accent family) and a daylight paper theme. A "House lights" switch in the masthead sets either, remembered per visitor.
o typefaces, two registers: serif to read, mono to label. No third font.
at surfaces; depth is tonal layering, hairlines and a 2px gold left edge.
e corner radius (3px) for every panel, card, input and chip.
ass is the only interactive colour; rust only flags; green only marks AI-written prose.

rules.name: The One Lamp Rule
rules.body: Gold is light, and there is one lamp. Belt Gold appears as text, a 1–3px edge or a wash at 10% alpha or less; never as a filled background, except the attestor credit badge.

rules.name: The Flag Colours Are Spoken For Rule
rules.body: Rust means a curation flag and green means AI-written prose. Neither is ever used for anything else, and no new hue is introduced: a new component reuses these tokens.

rules.name: The Two Registers Rule
rules.body: Serif reads, mono labels. Every `font-family` in the stylesheet reads `--font-serif` or `--font-mono`; there is no third stack and no web font.

rules.name: The One Row Size Rule
rules.body: Every list row, table cell and roster line uses the 16px row size, so sections sitting side by side on one page never read as different sizes.

rules.name: The Placard Column Rule
rules.body: Content lives in the one 760px column. A new page widens nothing; it uses the existing grids or a scrolling table wrap.

rules.name: The Lamplit Rule
rules.body: Light comes from above and only once. No drop shadows, no glows, no elevation on hover: a hover changes colour or an edge, never depth.

rules.name: The House Lights Rule
rules.body: The visitor's device decides until the visitor does. A theme is a set of token values, never a second set of component rules, and every text token clears 4.5:1 on every surface it sits on, in both themes.

dos: **Do** read every colour, size and space from the `:root` tokens in `style.css`; a new rule names a token, never a raw value.
**Do** add a new component as a class in `style.css` built from existing tokens, and document it in the stylesheet's header vocabulary.
**Do** keep the labels in the mono register: uppercase, tracked out (+0.08em to +0.34em), 11px or 12px.
**Do** use the 2px Retired Gold left edge for a museum label and the rust left edge for a curator's flag.
**Do** keep served documents in the mono document block with `pre-wrap`: formatting may be made more readable, the words never change.
**Do** honour `prefers-reduced-motion`; nothing animates, and the stylesheet keeps that promise explicitly.
donts: **Don't** add a `style=` attribute to any page; the validator fails it.
**Don't** load a web font or add a third font stack.
**Don't** add a `box-shadow`, a glow or a hover lift.
**Don't** introduce a new hue. Rust is only for flags and green is only for the AI flag.
**Don't** fill a large surface with gold; gold is text, an edge or a wash of 8% or less.
**Don't** bump the stylesheet's `?v=` query for purely additive rules; a bump re-stamps every page on the site.
**Don't** theme a component directly; add or retint a token in both theme blocks instead.
